issue_context.title: Bypassing Purpose/Trust Mechanism in X.509 Validation
issue_context.body:
OpenSSL Version: 1.1.1l

I'm parsing and checking an X.509 cert's Key Usage and Extended Key Usage fields manually. So I think I don't need OpenSSL's built-in purpose-checking and trust-checking mechanisms as they serve the same purpose with less accuracy (and I don't think they are implemented properly because of funny comments asking questions in relevant functions' code). So I want to completely disable purpose and trust checking for X509_verify_cert() and such similar functions. 

How can I accomplish that? Setting purpose to X509_PURPOSE_ANY using X509_STORE_CTX_set_purpose() doesn't seem to work.
comments:
> How can I accomplish that? Setting purpose to X509_PURPOSE_ANY using X509_STORE_CTX_set_purpose() doesn't seem to work.

Calling `X509_STORE_CTX_set_purpose()` using `X509_PURPOSE_ANY` should do what you need it to do. Can you elaborate more on the behaviour you are seeing?

It gives an error with string:
 
error:0B086079:x509 certificate routines:X509_STORE_CTX_purpose_inherit:unknown purpose id

Interesting! That looks like a bug to me. This might work as a workaround. Instead of:

````
X509_STORE_CTX_set_purpose(ctx, X509_PURPOSE_ANY);
````
Try:
````
X509_STORE_CTX_set_purpose_inherit(ctx, X509_PURPOSE_ANY, X509_PURPOSE_ANY, 0);
````
Note also that checking a purpose only occurs if a purpose has actually been set. So simply omitting a call to `X509_STORE_CTX_set_purpose` should also work.

@mattcaswell First of all thanks for the info and the patch. This seemed weird to me it's why I mentioned "funny comments asking questions" in OpenSSL code.

I will ask something more: Is there anything I need to do to disable trust checking? or is this enough for both purpose and trust?

Sorry for the slow response, I've been away on vacation.

> I will ask something more: Is there anything I need to do to disable trust checking? or is this enough for both purpose and trust?

Unless you do something else you will just get the default trust checking. I don't think there is an easy way to disable trust checking completely. Probably you could do it by adding a custom X509_TRUST object via `X509_TRUST_add` - but this appears to be undocumented and you would definitely be trailblazing if you went that route.
Hmm as I'm parsing and checking an X.509 cert's Key Usage and Extended Key Usage fields manually, do you think I need purpose & trust checking mechanisms at all?

If you don't have any certs with "Trust" settings then you don't need the trust features. Its unclear to me how widely used this feature is. I suspect hardly at all. At least my "/etc/ssl/certificates" store doesn't contain any certs with trust settings. That said if you don't have any certs with trust settings then I guess the built-in trust feature is harmless (i.e. a no-op).

The built-in purpose checking can do checks beyond just Key Usage and Extended Key Usage. I would be hesitant to completely remove the built-in checking with something custom without a very clear understanding of all the checks that the built-in support performs (you'd need to check the code for this).

review_comments: And for the archives, this is #17496 -- thanks for filing it.

I might consider adding a check for `def_purpose != 0` here instead of overwriting it above when it's zero, but as far as I can tell the two spellings are functionally equivalent for the current usage, and chances of adding further use of `def_purpose` in the future are slim, so there's not really much difference.
I've left this as-is for now.
Is the reasoning for not checking untrcert and trcert that we expect the subsequent APIs to handle the NULL input and error out?
No, the reasoning was I forgot to add them. Added now.
This would be somewhat annoying to refactor if we ever wanted to extend the test to look at more certs than just ee_cert.  But I'm willing to defer that problem to when the need should arise.
